prompts.text: What imaginary title would you give a travel documentary starring the two of us?
Tell me about a trip where one tiny surprise became our favourite story.
Plan a journey using a paper map or follow unusual local recommendations?
We have to create a travel guide using only places we've visited together. What's the funniest chapter?
Couples sometimes remember opposite details about the same holiday.
Being able to recover from travel mishaps together is a useful kind of romance.
Which place we've visited would you enjoy exploring again with no schedule?
Recall a time we misunderstood directions and ended up somewhere unexpectedly interesting.
We're allowed to pack only three nonessential items for a weekend away. What would you insist on taking?
A road trip with our favourite songs or a short train journey with a shared book?
What's an expression from your family you think I would misuse in a funny way?
Tell me about learning a word or phrase from each other and using it at the wrong moment.
Teach each other tongue-twisters or invent nicknames in a language we're learning?
We try to speak only in a language we're both beginners at for ten minutes. What goes wrong first?
A couple's private vocabulary often grows from small misunderstandings.
Learning each other's favourite phrases is more entertaining than memorising complicated speeches.
Which saying of mine have you unexpectedly started using yourself?
Recall a time one of us translated a joke badly and made it even funnier.
We have to write a postcard together using five words from different languages. What would we say?
A phrase-of-the-day challenge or a silly pronunciation contest?
If we adopted a pet with a mischievous personality, what would we call it?
Describe an animal encounter we shared that became a story you still retell.
Visit a farm together or volunteer at a local animal shelter for a day?
Our imaginary pet chooses its favourite person in the house. What clues would give it away?
Partners often disagree about whether an animal looks innocent or is plotting trouble.
Giving a pet a ridiculous nickname is almost inevitable when two people care for it.
Which animal do you think would copy your personality more closely than mine?
Tell me about seeing me react to an animal in a way you hadn't expected.
We design a tiny welcome sign for a pet's first day at home. What does it say?
A curious cat who investigates everything or a cheerful dog who loves visitors?
What would be the funniest way to assign us gardening responsibilities?
Recall trying to care for a plant and learning something surprising from the result.
Grow herbs we cook with or compete to grow the healthiest houseplant?
Our plants begin giving quarterly feedback on their caretakers. Who gets the better review?
The person who remembers watering schedules isn't always the one who chooses the plants.
A tiny shared garden is worth the effort even if the first harvest is unimpressive.
Which plant would you choose as a symbol of our different personalities?
Tell me about seeing something grow after we thought we'd made a mistake caring for it.
We have to design a balcony garden on a small budget. What would our first purchase be?
A weekend visit to a botanical garden or an afternoon planting seeds at home?
What board game would expose our different approaches to taking risks?
Describe a time one of us nearly won a game and made a spectacular final mistake.
Cooperate to solve a mystery game or compete in a ridiculous trivia contest?
We have to invent a game based on our house rules. What would count as a winning move?
Partners often discover how differently they handle competition when the stakes are imaginary.
A playful rematch is better than taking a friendly loss personally.
Which game would you want to teach me and then challenge me to beat you at?
Tell me about cheering each other on in a competition neither of us was good at.
Our friends ask us to enter a quiz as a couple. Which topic should we volunteer to answer?
Win a game as a team or have a close contest against each other?
What's an active weekend date that feels more like play than exercise?
Tell me about an outing where we discovered one of us had unexpected stamina.
A gentle bike ride or a beginner dance class with no spectators?
We decide to train together for a fun local event. How should we encourage each other?
Different fitness levels make shared activities easier when the goal is enjoyment, not competition.
An easy walk together is a legitimate date even if nobody records the distance.
Which physical activity would make us laugh more than it would make us sweat?
Recall a moment a friendly outdoor challenge brought out our silly sides.
Our first attempt at a new sport goes badly. What's the kindest way to suggest another try?
Learn a simple dance routine or try a casual doubles sport together?
Which fictional couple reminds you of our funniest disagreements?
Tell me about watching a film together and predicting completely different endings.
Take turns choosing surprise films or revisit a show we both quote often?
We're asked to dub the dialogue of a silent film together. What kind of characters would we play?
Couples sometimes recognise each other's reactions before a movie's funniest scene arrives.
Disagreeing about a fictional character is an excellent reason for a harmless debate.
Which book character would you most enjoy asking for relationship advice as a joke?
Recall a film recommendation from me that surprised you in a good way.
We each get to redesign the ending of a favourite story. Whose version would be more dramatic?
A cinema outing with a lively discussion afterwards or a quiet reading date?
What would you nominate as the funniest thing we've ever tried to save money on?
Describe a low-cost day together that ended up feeling more special than expected.
Plan a no-spend challenge for an afternoon or find the best free event in town?
We're each given a tiny budget to surprise the other with something thoughtful. What would you choose?
Couples sometimes discover their favourite treats cost much less than elaborate plans.
A thoughtful bargain isn't less meaningful than an expensive present.
Which free activity would you love to repeat with me every few months?
Tell me about us discovering that a simple idea was better than the original expensive plan.
We have to find a birthday gift for each other using only objects we've made. What's your idea?
A handmade scrapbook or an afternoon dedicated to teaching each other something useful?
Which relative do you think would win a playful two-person quiz about our relationship?
Tell me about your family discovering something amusing about the way we cooperate.
Host an informal family game or cook a shared dish with our relatives?
Our families challenge us to explain how we met in one minute each. Whose story would be more dramatic?
Families sometimes remember a couple's first meeting differently from the couple themselves.
The best family introductions let people be themselves rather than perform.
Which family tradition would be funniest to try for the first time together?
Recall somebody in our families making you feel welcome through an unexpected joke.
We plan a relaxed dinner bringing together relatives with different interests. What's one conversation starter?
Exchange favourite family recipes or trade childhood photographs with permission?
What playful tradition would you want us to start next year?
Describe a tiny celebration we made up without needing any special occasion.
Write future-us a funny letter or record one shared prediction each year?
We invent a time capsule containing five objects from our life together. Which unexpected item earns a place?
A relationship's history includes ordinary days that only the two people involved remember.
It's worth leaving space for new traditions instead of repeating everything automatically.
What's one imaginative challenge we could revisit every anniversary?
Tell me about a small choice we made together that became a lasting part of our routine.
We find a letter our younger selves wrote about love. How would we answer it together?
Make a new memory in a familiar place or visit somewhere entirely unexpected?
